description: Found investigating fz-sc8.225. Native registers every struct_schemas entry at load (native_codegen/driver.rs); interp registers a schema only the first time ProgramStep::Struct builds that struct (ir_interp/backend.rs, also register_exception and ir_interp/value.rs). So a map that spells S (e.g. Map.put(%{a: 1, b: [2]}, :__struct__, S)) printed before the first %S{} is built prints as a map on interp and as %S{...} on run and build. Register the program's schemas once at load on interp; construction stops registering. Done when: a fixture prints such a map before the first %S{} and matches Elixir on all three paths, and construction sites no longer call register_schema. Proposal: https://claude.ai/artifact/N14ZzKaX8vUSfrX4Uxx58t (ticket C).
title: Interp registers a program's struct schemas at load, as native does
